contrary_evidence: U.S. equities remained comparatively resilient despite the rates repricing.
Inventory and refinery data do not establish generalized physical scarcity; the strongest stress remains concentrated in middle distillates.
The transmission can weaken if long-end yields retrace or diesel cracks normalize.
limitations: Intraday market levels are time-sensitive snapshots.

publication.title: Rates, energy and the repricing of duration risk
publication.title_pt: Juros, energia e a reprecificação do risco de duration
publication.summary: Japan's 10-year government bond yield reached 3.055%, the highest since August 1996, while U.S. 10-year and 30-year Treasury yields moved to roughly 5.11% and 5.40%. At the same time, Brent rebounded to $103.08 a barrel and the European diesel crack remained near a record $95 a barrel. The combination matters more than either move in isolation: higher long-end discount rates and persistent energy costs are tightening financial conditions while leaving equity benchmarks comparatively resilient.
publication.summary_pt: O rendimento do título público japonês de 10 anos chegou a 3,055%, o maior nível desde agosto de 1996, enquanto os Treasuries americanos de 10 e 30 anos avançaram para cerca de 5,11% e 5,40%. Ao mesmo tempo, o Brent voltou a US$ 103,08 por barril e o crack spread europeu do diesel permaneceu próximo do recorde de US$ 95 por barril. A combinação importa mais do que cada movimento isolado: taxas longas mais altas e custos persistentes de energia apertam as condições financeiras enquanto os principais índices acionários permanecem relativamente resilientes.
publication.thesis: The dominant cross-asset change is no longer simply expensive oil. It is the interaction between a global long-end bond selloff and an energy shock concentrated in middle distillates. Japan's 10-year JGB at 3.055% and U.S. long bonds above 5% raise the discount rate applied to long-duration assets, while diesel scarcity transmits into freight, industrial and household costs. The central question is whether that combination becomes a durable tightening regime or remains a short-lived geopolitical and positioning shock.
publication.key_risk: A persistent combination of long-end yield repricing and elevated middle-distillate margins would tighten financial conditions and production costs simultaneously, raising the probability of weaker demand without an immediate normalization of inflation-sensitive prices.
publication.primary_mechanism: Energy supply disruption -> higher diesel and crude prices -> transport and industrial cost pressure -> firmer inflation expectations and term premium -> higher long-end sovereign yields -> tighter financial conditions and valuation pressure.
publication.regime: Global markets are in a rates-energy tightening regime: sovereign curves are repricing higher while energy-product scarcity remains acute, but equity indices have not yet validated a broad risk-off transition.
